svg.aria-label: so 2 of 9 events are in the wrong bucket
svg.text: Three shapes through one function — only the key changes
bounded and streaming group identically · batch misplaces ids 6, 7
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which is the whole subject of ch01:
3 // et = event time, when the thing happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being summed (clicks, here) · key = which stream it belongs to
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
8 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the late one
9 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
10 // primitive: MIN — seconds in a dashboard minute. MIN = 60
11 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
12 // primitive: minOf(sec) — the START of the MIN-second minute holding sec.
14 // primitive: add(m, k, n) — add n to m[k], starting from 0 when k is absent.
16 // primitive: keysOf(m) — m's keys, ascending. keysOf({0: 12, 60: 7}) = [0, 60]
20 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds of EVENT time. WIN = 120
21 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the WIN-second EVENT-time window holding et.
23 // primitive: chunkOf(pt) — the START of the WIN-second PROCESSING-time slice holding pt.
25 // primitive: append(m, k, id) — append id to the list at m[k], creating it if absent.
28 // function: keyFor(e, shape) — the ONE line that differs between the three shapes.
37 // function: group(events, shape) — bucket every event under keyFor.
50 // function: watermarkAfter(i) — as in the previous concept: the highest event
51 // time through i, minus LAG. watermarkAfter(4) = 185
61 // function: closesAt(shape, winStart) — the event index after which that
62 // window's answer is final. For bounded that is always end-of-input.
74 // function: misplaced(events) — events whose batch slice is not their window.
84 // function: main() — THE CALLER: three shapes, one function each time.
Step 3/0 — so 2 of 9 events are in the wrong bucket
`bad` = [6, 7] — 22% of the dataset. Compare the two Grouping rows at key 240: batch holds [4,5,6,7], the windows hold [4,5]. This function can only compute that because it
sees both clocks; a batch chunk, from the inside, cannot.
